title: The New Opportunity
content:
Sophie had worked at a small marketing company for almost three years. She enjoyed her job, but recently she had started to feel that she needed a new challenge.

One Monday morning, her manager, Mr. Carter, asked her to come to his office.

— Sophie, do you have a minute?

— Of course. Is everything okay?

— Everything is fine. In fact, I have some good news. One of our biggest clients has opened a new position, and I think you could be the right person for it.

Sophie was surprised.

— Are you offering me the position?

— Not exactly. They still have to interview several candidates, but I recommended you.

Sophie felt excited, but also nervous. The new position would involve managing a small team and working directly with important clients.

— It sounds like a great opportunity, but I'm not sure I'm ready.

Mr. Carter smiled.

— You have more experience than you think. You just need to trust yourself.

That afternoon, Sophie updated her résumé and prepared for the interview. She researched the company, reviewed her previous projects, and wrote down some questions she wanted to ask.

Two days later, she arrived at the company's modern office. The interview went well, but one question made her think carefully.

— Where do you see yourself in five years? — the director asked.

Sophie took a moment before answering.

— I would like to lead a team, develop new ideas, and help the company grow. I also want to continue learning.

The director nodded.

— That's an interesting answer. What makes you think you can achieve those goals?

Sophie thought about everything she had learned during the past three years.

— I've made mistakes, but I've learned from them. I've worked with different clients, solved difficult problems, and learned how to work under pressure. I believe those experiences have prepared me for the next step.

A few days later, Sophie received a phone call.

— Hello, Sophie? This is Mr. Adams from the company. We'd like to offer you the position.

She couldn't help smiling.

— Thank you! I'd be very happy to accept it.

After hanging up, Sophie immediately called Mr. Carter.

— I got the job!

— I knew you would.

— Thank you for recommending me.

— You earned it. Now it's time for your next challenge.

Sophie looked at her desk and thought about how much her professional life was going to change. She knew the new job wouldn't be easy, but she was ready to learn, make mistakes, and grow.

Sometimes, a new opportunity doesn't arrive when we feel completely prepared. It arrives when we are ready to take the risk and discover what we are capable of.
